questions.question: What does `const [addFund, result] = useAddFundMutation()` do when the component renders?
options: Nothing is sent until you call addFund(...)
questions.explanation: Mutation hooks return a trigger function and the latest result. The request is sent only when the trigger is called.

questions.question: Why does the getFunds list query also provide a `{ type: "Fund", id: "LIST" }` tag?
options: RTK Query requires every query to provide a LIST tag
It makes the list load faster
It limits how many items the list holds
So that adding a new item, whose id is not in any cached query yet, can invalidate the list
questions.explanation: A newly created item cannot match any existing per-id tag. Invalidating the LIST tag tells RTK Query that the collection itself has changed.

questions.question: getFunds provides per-id tags plus LIST, and getFund(2) provides Fund/2. Both are subscribed. Which queries refetch after a mutation that invalidates `{ type: "Fund", id: 2 }`?
options: Neither; you must call refetch manually
questions.explanation: Every subscribed query that provides the invalidated tag refetches. The list provides Fund/2 for its item, and the detail query provides it too.

questions.question: What does `invalidatesTags: ["Fund"]` (the bare type, no id) do?
options: Invalidates only queries that provided the bare "Fund" tag
Throws, because an id is required
Invalidates every Fund tag, whatever its id
questions.explanation: Invalidating a bare tag type matches every tag of that type, so all Fund queries refetch. This is simple but coarse.
